catalog_quote: Chorote has contrastive stress. In our proposal, Iyo’awujwa’ and Manjui are conservative with regard to the position of the stress, whereas Iyojwa’aja’ underwent stress retraction in some cases, as will be shown in §8.2.4. Synchronically, the stress of any given Chorote word form can be determined based on the accentual properties of individual morphemes as follows. The leftmost underlying accent is the one that appears in the surface realization, whereas all subsequent accents are deleted. If no morpheme in a given Chorote word contains an underlying accent, a default accent is inserted in the peninitial syllable (or in the only syllable in the case of monosyllabic words). ... (522) Manjui (Carol 2018, Hunt 1994) a. /hl-úp-ís/ [ˈhlʊpis] ... ‘its nests’ ... d. /ʔis-ís/ [ʔaxˈseis] ... ‘they are good’ ... g. /kihwijh/ [kiˈhwijh] ... ‘inside, below, beneath’ ... m. /s-kihwijh/ [ʃiˈkeihwi] …

sources.quote: 'Estas [vocales] tienden a ser más laxas cuando reciben el acento de intensidad; /i/ tónica diptonga en [ei̯, ǝi̯] o bien se abre en [ɪ] ... El acento no puede predecirse; cae lo más frecuentemente en la primera sílaba del tema, con menos frecuencia en la segunda y, más raramente, en sufijos. En la notación utilizada en el presente trabajo, si no hay indicación explícita (´) cae en la primera sílaba del tema.'
sources.locator: sec. 2.1 'Sistema fonológico', p. 108 (variety V2E = Manjui of Santa Rosa/Wonta, Abizai etc., Paraguay; dialect classification pp. 106-107, Cuadro 1)
sources.note: Newest first-hand phonological description of Manjui (V2E) by the fieldworker; sec. 2.1 states stress is unpredictable (most often stem-initial, less often second syllable, rarely on suffixes) — independent confirmation of the LEXICAL coding for the Paraguayan half of iyow1239.
